description.p: A 180 GB archive that unpacks to 200 GB normally needs 380 GB of free disk, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB: it extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files.

ul.li: Checks that the extraction fits before it changes anything
Keeps a margin of free space the whole way through
Can be stopped or crash at any moment and continues where it left off
Reads ZIP, 7z, tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz and split archives

description.p: The archive is gone when the extraction finishes, unless you choose to keep it. For an archive that cannot be downloaded again, HatchZip can verify every file first.
This build does not read RAR archives: the RAR decoder, UnRAR, is not free software. RAR archives are refused before anything is changed.
The hatchzip command line tool is included and runs with flatpak run --command=hatchzip io.github.xevrion.hatchzip.

ul.li: When an .sfv file named after the archive is next to it, every volume is checked against it before anything is modified
ZIP archives made with zip on Linux and macOS extract with the right file times, using the UTC times they store
Files dated before 1970 in a tar archive are read correctly
A ZIP entry named like folder/.. is refused before anything is touched
The Open dialog lists archives with upper-case extensions
Replace, Skip or Keep both for each file already in the destination
The progress window closes when the extraction completes, unless turned off in Settings
Existing files you chose to keep are moved aside first and moved back at the end, so a crash never loses one

description.p: Fixes two security issues, GHSA-cq63-4gv9-w2gc and GHSA-m6m5-qcjx-55gv.

ul.li: Files already in the destination can be replaced, and are kept aside until the extraction completes
Check for updates in the Help menu opens the latest release page in the browser

description.p: Fixes a security issue, GHSA-446w-m5mg-2f58: progress files placed next to an archive are checked before a resume uses them.

ul.li: Extract and keep the archive, with nothing removed
Opening a large ZIP no longer reads the whole archive first
